_readme: All the text on the site is in this file. The site reads it; nothing here is shown except what is under 'site' and 'designs'.
Change the text between the quotes and leave the names on the left of each colon as they are.
Each text stays on one line. A double quote inside a text needs a backslash in front of it.
'site' is shared by every design: services, principles, numbers, industries, insights, the brief, the lede and the About page.
'designs' is each design's own wording. Its desktop page and its phone page both use it, so a change here shows on both.
A phone page may leave a piece out: it has no Insights or Industries sections, no section paragraphs and no contact points. Natt's phone hero shows site.brief; its desktop hero shows site.lede.
In a heading, 'kicker' is the small label above the title and 'accent' is the rest of the title in the accent colour. Leave either out for none.
Signal's approach title and Grense's ai kicker and title are shown on the phone only.
Limits: Natt's heroTitle plus heroTitleAccent may be 60 characters and site.brief 180 (the phone hero must stay short); site.about.summary should stay under 160.
A service's code starts with two letters that pick its icon: AI, RM, TI, VC, RG, FT, CX or TR.
site.stats are placeholder figures: replace them with real ones before launch. Text in [square brackets] is a placeholder for your own details.
To check the file after a change, run: go test ./...   To see changes on a browser refresh, run: go run . -dev

site.name: Wintermute Consulting OÜ
site.brief: Boutique AI, cyber and ICT risk advisory with a special focus on regulated financial institutions across the European Union: from board-approved policy to implemented, auditable controls, and reporting.
site.lede: A boutique team of senior advisors helping financial institutions across the European Union meet emerging AI and cyber threats. We build the complete stack, from board-approved policy to implemented, auditable controls, sized to your organisation and your risk appetite, and rest easier through the long nights.
site.location: Serving clients across the European Union

services.title: Emerging AI: threats, security & governance
services.body: Offensive and defensive AI. How attackers now use it, from deepfakes and  AI-executed spear phishing to the increased inherent cyber risk due to rapidly advancing fronteir models. What it means for your orginziation and how to defend with it. We help institutions build the AI policy stack and controls, and govern the AI your institution deploys under the EU AI Act and DORA.

services.title: Custom frameworks & controls
services.body: Your own information security and ICT risk management framework, not a template: we help you build the complete stack from board-approved policy to standards, procedures and implemented controls, built on DORA and its regulatory technical standards, NIS2, ISO/IEC 27001, NIST CSF 2.0 and NIST SP 800-53, mapped to local regulation, and sized to your organisation and risk appetite.

services.title: Threat intelligence & geopolitical risk
services.body: Emerging cyber threats and the geopolitical drivers behind them: state-aligned intrusion, hacktivism, sanctions, conflict and supply-chain exposure, translated into scenarios, control changes and briefings your management body can act on.

services.title: Virtual CISO
services.body: Fractional or interim security leadership for a single institution or across a private equity portfolio. We own the security programme, report to your management body and represent it before your supervisor, for as long as you need us.

services.title: Regulatory audits & remediation
services.body: Audits and inspection readiness under DORA, the ECB's supervisory expectations and NIS2, integrated with the national rules of your member state: every requirement traced to a control and its evidence, and remediation programmes that close the findings.

services.title: Fintech advisory
services.body: For founders and early teams: a policy stack and controls sized to your stage, built in from the licence application onwards, and ready for the supervisor, your banking partners and investor due diligence.

services.title: Crisis exercises
services.body: Tabletop exercises and crisis simulations built on today's threats (a deepfaked CFO, a state-aligned outage, a critical provider gone dark) for management bodies, investment committees and crisis teams, with a debrief that shows who must decide what.

services.title: Training
services.body: Security and digital operational resilience training matched to the role: awareness for all staff, including recognising AI-enabled social engineering, specialist sessions for control functions, and briefings for members of the management body.

principles.title: Sized to you
principles.body: Not every institution is in the same place. Frameworks and controls are fitted to your size, complexity and risk appetite, as DORA's proportionality principle intends, never copied from a template.

principles.title: Auditable end to end
principles.body: Every requirement traced from regulation to policy, control and evidence, so your auditor and your supervisor can follow the thread.

principles.title: Boutique by design
principles.body: Senior advisors only, with no leverage pyramid and no hand-offs. The advisor who scopes your engagement is the one in the room with your management body.

principles.title: Discretion
principles.body: We never publish client names or discuss our work, we don't sell data, and this site sets no cookies.

stats.label: EU member states, one DORA rulebook

industries.name: Banking
industries.body: Credit institutions under ECB and national supervision, preparing for inspections and meeting DORA's requirements for ICT risk management.

industries.name: Fintech & payments
industries.body: Payment and e-money institutions and fintech startups, from the first licence application to scale, with security sized to the stage.

industries.name: Private equity
industries.body: General partners and their portfolio companies: cyber due diligence before signing, a remediation plan in the first hundred days, and a clean account of security at exit.

industries.name: SME institutional holders
industries.body: Small and mid-sized institutional holders, from holding companies and foundations to smaller pension and endowment funds: institutional assets and obligations, run by a lean team.

industries.name: Wealth & asset management
industries.body: Boutique wealth managers and funds meeting allocators' operational due diligence and their supervisors' expectations with a lean team.

industries.name: Trading & digital assets
industries.body: Investment firms, trading venues and crypto-asset service providers under MiCA, where availability, custody and third-party infrastructure are regulatory questions.

insights.title: The CFO's voice is not the CFO: deepfakes in the treasury
insights.summary: How AI-generated voice and video now drive payment fraud, and the call-back and approval controls that still stop it.

insights.title: Your AI policy stack: from risk appetite to controls an auditor can test
insights.summary: What the management body should decide about AI, how that becomes policy, and the controls that prove it is being followed.

insights.title: Geopolitics is now an ICT risk driver
insights.summary: Why supervisors expect sanctions, conflict and state-aligned activity to appear in your ICT risk assessment, and the questions your management body should ask.
